title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis in aging
bottleneck: The aged gut microbiome loses diversity, gains pro-inflammatory taxa, and the intestinal barrier leaks microbial products that fuel systemic inflammaging. But causality is murky: does dysbiosis drive aging, or does aging drive dysbiosis? Fecal transplants from young donors rejuvenate aged mice, yet human data are correlative and strain-specific effects are unknown.
why_it_blocks: The microbiome is the most modifiable aging lever (diet, probiotics, transplant), but without causal maps, interventions are shots in the dark, and commercial probiotics outrun evidence.
current_state: Microbiome profiling is a research tool; defined bacterial consortia are in early trials for C. difficile and metabolic endpoints, not aging. Diet and exercise remain the only evidence-based modulators. Defined bacterial consortia and engineered probiotics are in early trials, but the field cannot yet predict which strains engraft, persist, or causally shift host aging phenotypes.
